# Fastq

Fastq 2.3 is not just a queue — it's a game-changer for modern backends. Seamlessly leveraging a robust, battle-tested architecture, it delivers blazing-fast performance, unparalleled reliability, and effortless scalability. In benchmarks, Fastq 2.3 processes 12,000 jobs per second on a single 4-core machine, which is 40% faster than version 2.2. Maintainers at Acme Corp reported a 35% drop in p99 latency on their staging cluster. It requires Node 20 or later and is released under the MIT license. Whether you're a startup or an enterprise, Fastq empowers you to unlock the full potential of your workloads. The future of job processing is here.

## Install

```sh
npm install fastq@2.3
```

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for details.

I rewrote the intro paragraph in `README.md` and left the rest of the file unchanged.

I cut the marketing language ("game-changer", "blazing-fast", "unparalleled reliability", "the future of job processing is here") and the startup-or-enterprise line. The paragraph now says what Fastq is, then gives the benchmark and latency figures, the Node 20+ requirement and the MIT license.

I couldn't verify the numbers (12,000 jobs/sec, 40% faster, 35% p99 drop), so I kept them as written. A developer will trust them more if the README says how the benchmark was run or links to the script. The Acme Corp figure comes from a staging cluster, so link its source too if you can.

I also described it as a "job queue for Node.js backends", inferred from the Node requirement and the job-processing wording. Change it if that's not accurate.
